title: Gas sensor network with rescue escalation (Timed Rebeca case study)
source: Timed Rebeca sensor network case study. Aceto, Cimini, Ingolfsdottir, Reynisson, Sigurdarson and Sirjani, FOCLASA 2011 (EPTCS 58), Section 5 and Listing 5; journal version Reynisson et al., Science of Computer Programming 89 (2014) 41-68, Table 3 (p. 56) and Listing 6, which the --table3-row presets follow. The "published model" cells use the constants of the model file sensornetwork.rebeca on rebeca-lang.org (netDelay 1, sensor period 10, admin check 15, scientist deadline 5, admin rescue deadline 5, obstacle 0 or 1). The papers state no closed-form timing rule; the two laws are the example's own (header comment of the source file).
property: No false alarm at the Admin: once it has read every message sent to it, it must not have recorded a sensor failure (no sensor ever breaks in this model) nor a dead scientist (the scientist always answers and the rescue team always arrives); --property selects which of the two is asserted.
citable_note: The audit of 2026-09-18 said citable with caveats, and that still holds for the current source: one program for both modes, both properties can fail, and v9 reproduces all six Table 3 verdicts. Caveats: (1) every published-model hold is weak on its own (no rescue is ever sent, no reading is ever late; the binary prints a NOTE), so quote it beside the row 2, row 4 and D-safe holds; (2) Table 3 is ten simulation runs per row, the holds here are bounded by R, and rows 3-6 and 3-7 fail only at R=4, shown on the reduced one-sensor model; (3) quote the tool's violating executions, not the event counters, and never the execution counts printed in the source header (they predate lossy sends); (4) the cells named exact compare different --readings values on the two sides.
config_timed: build_config, sensor_network_timed.rs lines 1222 to 1238: Config::builder().with_all_sends_lossy().with_progress_report(usize::MAX) (line 1223), then .with_timed(L, U, sd).build() (line 1236). Consistency model FIFO (library default, the example never calls with_cons_type). Global transit window [L, U], storage sd (0 in every v9 cell); the Admin's alarms and timers are sent with an exact per-send transit (send_msg_timed(d, d), lines 982, 1091, 1098, 1286). Every send is lossy, without a budget. Every receive is a blocking timed receive (recv_msg_block_timed), there is no timeout. --keep-going adds with_keep_going_after_error(true) (lines 1229 to 1233). Scheduling policy LTR (library default); seed random per process (library default, no --seed flag). --parallel none (default) is sequential; --parallel partitioned adds with_partitioned_parallelization(true) (line 1227), with RAYON_NUM_THREADS set by the campaign to the cores of the job.
config_baseline: The same builder without with_timed (line 1235): Config::builder().with_all_sends_lossy().with_progress_report(usize::MAX).build(). FIFO, every send lossy without a budget, LTR, random seed; keep-going and parallel options as on the timed side. Transit bounds, exact timer transits and sleeps carry no meaning without the clock.
program_differs_between_modes: no: build_config is the only code that depends on the mode. But --readings random-relevant is refused in baseline mode (main, line 1771, exit 2), so in the five cells named exact with two sides the timed side runs random-relevant and the baseline side runs random: different arguments for the same model.
failing_tasks: Only the Admin thread asserts (lines 1210 and 1214, its last statements, after the drain). It is an unnamed spawned thread, so its line is task-3 with --timers self (main 0, Scientist 1, Rescue 2, Admin 3, then the sensors) and task-5 with --timers separate, i.e. in every --table3-row cell (the two timer threads take 3 and 4). The main thread never asserts. One line per violating execution, also when both verdicts fail in it.

counters.meaning: missions whose rescue timer found no RescueReach (false deaths), summed over all executions in which the Admin finished its drain. With R=1 there is at most one mission per execution, so with --property rescue it equals the violating executions. With R >= 2 it can exceed them, and with --property both the violating executions also include those with a sensor failure

(sensor, check) pairs in which a check found no report since the previous check, summed over all executions in which the Admin finished its drain. Counted whatever --property asserts, so it is above zero in rescue-property cells where nothing of the kind is asserted (Table 3 row 3: the first check comes before the first report)

readings read after a check they could have been read before (computed from the send index, P, L, C and sd, never from a clock). Not a violation: above zero on a hold it shows the hold is not vacuous. On the baseline it changes with L although the exploration does not
endings that admit no timeline (timeline_impossible). 0 in every v9 run of this example; if it were above zero, dead, sensor_failures and late_reports would be upper bounds

param_columns.meaning: Row of Table 3 of the SCP 2014 paper whose timer values the cell uses (--table3-row): 1, 2, 3-5, 3-6, 3-7 (row 3 with rescue deadline 5, 6 or 7) or 4; '-' for the cells on the published rebeca-lang.org timers and their two law-boundary variants
number of admin check periods: the Admin's CheckSensors alarm rings R times, at C, 2C, ..., RC (--rounds)

number of readings each sensor sends, floor((R*C + sd) / P) + 2 (the last one is sent after the last check can be read); a/b = sensor 0 / sensor 1 when their periods differ. Derived from R, C and P, not a flag. It is the size the published-model ladder grows: 4, 5, 7 readings at P = 6, 5, 3

gas values the sensors report (--readings): danger = always dangerous, every check that saw a report starts a mission; random = the paper's free choice between safe and dangerous on every reading; random-relevant = random on the readings a check can observe, fixed on the others (exact, timed mode only); safe = never dangerous, no mission starts. Where the two sides of a cell differ, both values are given
asserted verdicts (--property): sensor = no false sensor failure; rescue = no false death; both = the two together. Both verdicts are always counted, whatever is asserted
lower bound of the transit time of a message between two threads (round(--l-ratio x U)); ignored by the baseline
upper bound of the transit time (--u); L = U is the paper's fixed netDelay; ignored by the baseline
storage: how long a message stays readable after it arrives (round(--sd-ratio x U)); 0 in every cell, i.e. a message is readable only at its arrival instant, as in Timed Rebeca

time between two readings of a sensor; a/b = sensor 0 / sensor 1 when they differ (round(--period-ratio x U), --sensor0-period-ratio, --sensor1-period-ratio). A timer, but also the knob of the published-model ladder: a smaller P gives more readings per sensor, which is why the column is marked as moving with N
adminCheckDelay: the Admin looks at the readings every C ticks (round(--check-ratio x U))
scientistDeadline: time the Admin waits for the scientist's Ack after a warning (round(--ack-deadline-ratio x U)); not exercised with safe readings
Admin rescueDeadline: time the Admin waits for the rescue team's call after sending it (round(--rescue-deadline-ratio x U)); not exercised with safe readings
the rescue team is held up for 0 or OBST ticks, a free choice on every rescue (round(--obstacle-ratio x U)); not exercised with safe readings

how the Admin's two mission timers reach it (--timers): self = messages on the Admin's own channel (missions must not overlap); separate = one extra thread per timer kind, so timers ring in due-time order as in Timed Rebeca (set by --table3-row; needs sd = 0)

boundary_law: Two laws, both the example's own (header comment of the source; the papers publish no closed form), stated and grid-checked for one sensor and non-overlapping missions. False death: violation iff Ds <= 2U + 2sd and Dr <= 2U + 2sd + OBST (L plays no role). False sensor failure: violation iff C <= U + sd, or some check j in 2..R has (m+1)P + U + sd >= jC with m = floor(((j-1)C + sd - L) / P). Equality is on the violating side: a message that arrives when a timer rings may be handled after it. For the Table 3 rows the header adds the overlapping-mission failure, possible iff 2C <= Dr - 2 netDelay and only from 4 rounds on. How well checked: per the header, automated grids of 2026-09-16 (death law 216 and 72 cells, sensor law 576 cells, no disagreement), run with one sensor before every send became lossy. v9 has sd = 0 everywhere, so the sd terms are not exercised; it confirms both sides of one death boundary (regimes B, C), of one sensor boundary (D, E) and the six Table 3 rows (F to K) with two sensors.

regimes.name: Published model: exact netDelay 1, published alarm timers
regimes.params: L=U=1, sd=0, C=15, Ds=5, Dr=5, OBST=1, timers on the Admin's own channel (self); sensor period P=10 as published, or P=6, 5, 3 (more readings per sensor: the size lever of the P ladder)
regimes.rule: Death law: Ds=5 > 2U=2, the Ack is back 2 ticks after the warning, 3 ticks before the ack timer, so no rescue is ever sent. Sensor law: C=15 > U=1, and at P=10 every check j up to R=6 has (m+1)P + U < jC (21<30, 31<45, 51<60, 61<75, 81<90). The P=6, 5, 3 cells have R=1, where only C <= U + sd could violate.
regimes.expect_timed: 0 violations (no false sensor failure, no false death)
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations: without a clock an alarm can be read before the reading it waits for and a timer before the reply; false sensor failures in every cell and false deaths where readings are danger

regimes.name: Death-law boundary, safe side: published timers, netDelay 2
regimes.params: L=U=2, sd=0, P=6, C=15, Ds=5, Dr=5, OBST=1 (CLI ratios over U=2), timers self, danger readings, both properties
regimes.rule: First gate of the death law fails: Ds=5 > 2U=4. The Ack is back at 4, one tick before the ack timer, so no rescue is sent. One step of U below regime C.
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations: without a clock an alarm can be read before the reading it waits for and a timer before the reply; the same counts as the published P=6 baseline, the baseline does not see U

regimes.name: Death-law boundary, violating side: published timers, netDelay 3
regimes.params: L=U=3, sd=0, P=6, C=15, Ds=5, Dr=5, OBST=1 (CLI ratios over U=3), timers self, danger readings, both properties
regimes.rule: Both gates of the death law hold: Ds=5 <= 2U=6 (the Ack is back at 6, after the ack timer at 5) and Dr=5 <= 2U+OBST=7 (the rescue call is back at 6 or 7, after the rescue timer at 5). No tie is involved: every mission ends in a false death.
regimes.expect_baseline: violations; the same counts as in regime B and as the published P=6 baseline

regimes.name: Sensor-law boundary, safe side: a reading takes 0 to 4 ticks
regimes.params: L=0, U=4, sd=0, P=10, C=15 (CLI ratios over U=4), R=3, safe readings, sensor property; Ds=Dr=20 and OBST=4 follow from the default ratios and are never used
regimes.rule: Sensor law: C=15 > U, and (m+1)P + U < jC for both later checks (j=2: 24 < 30; j=3: 44 < 45). Reading 4, sent at 40, is in by 44, one tick before check 3. One step of U below regime E.
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations: without a clock an alarm can be read before the reading it waits for and a timer before the reply (false sensor failures only: safe readings start no mission)

regimes.name: Sensor-law boundary, violating side: a reading takes 0 to 5 ticks
regimes.params: L=0, U=5, sd=0, P=10, C=15 (CLI ratios over U=5), R=3, safe readings, sensor property; Ds=Dr=25 and OBST=5 are never used
regimes.rule: Sensor law at check 3: m=3 and (m+1)P + U = 45 >= 3C = 45. Reading 3 (sent at 30) can be read at 30 just before check 2 and reading 4 (sent at 40) at 45 just after check 3; equality counts because a message that arrives when the alarm rings may be handled after it. Needs R >= 3.
regimes.expect_baseline: violations; the same counts as in regime D

regimes.name: Table 3 row 1 (paper: mission failed)
regimes.params: netDelay 1 (L=U=1), sd=0, C=4, sensor periods 2 and 3, Ds=2, Dr=3, OBST=1, separate timer threads, rescue property
regimes.rule: Zero-margin ties on both gates of the death law: Ds = 2 netDelay = 2, so the Ack arrives at the instant the ack timer rings and may be handled after it, and Dr = 2 netDelay + OBST = 3, the same for the rescue call when the obstacle is taken. Violating from R=1.
regimes.expect_baseline: violations; the same counts as in regime G (row 2), the baseline does not see Dr

regimes.name: Table 3 row 2 (paper: mission success)
regimes.params: netDelay 1 (L=U=1), sd=0, C=4, sensor periods 2 and 3, Ds=2, Dr=4, OBST=1, separate timer threads, rescue property
regimes.rule: Row 1 with Dr=4 > 2 netDelay + OBST = 3: the rescue call is back at least one tick before the rescue timer. The Ack tie remains, so rescues are sent and all arrive in time. A bounded result: checked for R=1 and R=2.
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations: without a clock an alarm can be read before the reading it waits for and a timer before the reply; the same counts as in regime F (row 1)

regimes.name: Table 3 row 3 with rescue deadline 5 (paper: mission failed)
regimes.params: netDelay 2 (L=U=2), sd=0, C=1, sensor periods 1 and 1, Ds=4, Dr=5, OBST=1, separate timer threads, rescue property, R >= 2
regimes.rule: The tie race of row 1: Ds = 2 netDelay = 4 and Dr = 2 netDelay + OBST = 5. Needs R >= 2: with C=1 the first check (t=1) comes before the first report (t=2), so R=1 starts no mission.

regimes.name: Table 3 row 3 with rescue deadline 6, at most 3 rounds (bounded hold)
regimes.params: netDelay 2 (L=U=2), sd=0, C=1, sensor periods 1 and 1, Ds=4, Dr=6, OBST=1, separate timer threads, rescue property, R=2 or 3
regimes.rule: No single-mission race: Dr=6 > 2 netDelay + OBST = 5. The failure the paper reports for this row is the overlapping-mission one, which needs three missions, i.e. checks 2, 3 and 4, so it cannot happen within 3 rounds. Safe for this bound only; R=4 is regime I-viol.
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations: without a clock an alarm can be read before the reading it waits for and a timer before the reply

regimes.name: Table 3 row 3 with rescue deadline 6, 4 rounds (paper: mission failed)
regimes.params: mission timers of I-safe (L=U=2, sd=0, C=1, Ds=4, Dr=6, OBST=1), R=4; run on the reduced model: one sensor with period 100, danger readings
regimes.rule: Overlapping missions: 2C = 2 <= Dr - 2 netDelay = 2. A rescued mission's late Ack makes the next check count as acknowledged, so rescues are two checks apart; the rescues of missions 2 and 4 overlap and their two RescueReach messages land on the one flag scientistReached, which the first rescue timer consumes.
regimes.expect_timed: violation (false death), certified at the first one

regimes.name: Table 3 row 3 with rescue deadline 7, at most 3 rounds (bounded hold)
regimes.params: netDelay 2 (L=U=2), sd=0, C=1, sensor periods 1 and 1, Ds=4, Dr=7, OBST=1, separate timer threads, rescue property, R=2 or 3
regimes.rule: As I-safe with Dr=7 > 5: the overlapping-mission failure needs checks 2, 3 and 4. Safe for this bound only; R=4 is regime J-viol.
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations: without a clock an alarm can be read before the reading it waits for and a timer before the reply

regimes.name: Table 3 row 3 with rescue deadline 7, 4 rounds (paper: mission failed)
regimes.params: mission timers of J-safe (L=U=2, sd=0, C=1, Ds=4, Dr=7, OBST=1), R=4; run on the reduced model: one sensor with period 100, danger readings
regimes.rule: Overlapping missions as in I-viol: 2C = 2 <= Dr - 2 netDelay = 3.
regimes.expect_timed: violation (false death), certified at the first one

regimes.name: Table 3 row 4 (paper: mission success)
regimes.params: netDelay 2 (L=U=2), sd=0, C=4, sensor periods 1 and 1, Ds=4, Dr=7, OBST=1, separate timer threads, rescue property, R=1
regimes.rule: No single-mission race (Dr=7 > 2 netDelay + OBST = 5) and no overlapping-mission failure (2C = 8 > Dr - 2 netDelay = 3). A bounded result: checked for R=1 only.
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations: without a clock an alarm can be read before the reading it waits for and a timer before the reply

glossary.meaning: the integer time unit of the model. Every timer column is in ticks; the CLI takes ratios over U and rounds the product.
the fixed message delay of the paper's model. Here it is the transit window [L, U]; L = U = netDelay in every cell except regimes D and E (L = 0).

the threads of the model: the sensors report gas readings to the Admin every P ticks; the Admin checks them every C ticks, warns the Scientist when a reading is dangerous and sends the Rescue team when the Scientist does not answer in time.

what a check starts when the latest reading of some sensor is dangerous: the Admin warns the scientist and arms the ack timer (Ds); if no Ack was handled when it rings, it sends the rescue team and arms the rescue timer (Dr).

the Admin records the scientist as dead although the scientist answered and the rescue team arrived: their messages were handled after the timers. The paper's "mission failed". Asserted by --property rescue and both.
a check finds no report from a sensor since the previous check although no sensor ever breaks in this model. Asserted by --property sensor and both.

harness rule: the Admin keeps receiving until it has read every message sent to it and asserts only then. An execution in which some message can no longer be read (passed over, or dropped by the lossy network) blocks and reaches no assertion; this is why blocked counts are large on both sides.

the Admin blocks as soon as it reads a message out of its channel's send order, since such an execution could never finish the drain (cut=on in the summary line; it saves work and changes no count of complete executions, per the source header).

harness messages the Admin sends after its drain to release the Scientist, the Rescue team and the timer threads. They are lossy like every send: an execution in which one is dropped ends blocked, also when it violates.
false death possible iff Ds <= 2U + 2sd and Dr <= 2U + 2sd + OBST (the example's own rule, one sensor, non-overlapping missions). Regimes B and C are its two sides.
false sensor failure possible iff C <= U + sd, or some check j in 2..R has (m+1)P + U + sd >= jC with m = floor(((j-1)C + sd - L) / P) (the example's own rule). Regimes D and E are its two sides.
a message that arrives at the very instant a timer or alarm rings may be handled before or after it; both orders are explored, and the late order is what makes Table 3 rows 1 and 3-5 fail.

Table 3 of Reynisson et al., Science of Computer Programming 89 (2014), p. 56: six timer settings with the verdict of ten McErlang simulation runs each ("mission failed" or "mission success"). --table3-row loads one setting; row 3 lists three rescue deadlines and is split into 3-5, 3-6 and 3-7.
in cell names: --table3-row with no override, i.e. two sensors, random readings, obstacle 0 or 1, rescue property, separate timers.
in cell names: the Listing 6 model with random readings, explored exhaustively by the timed side through --readings random-relevant.

an exact reduction of random readings for the timed mode with L = U and sd = 0: a reading whose value no check can observe is fixed to safe. Each reduced execution stands for 2^k full ones, k = number of fixed readings (4 in rows 1 and 2 at R=1, 8 in row 4). Refused in baseline mode, where a fixed reading could be the last one a check sees.

in cell names: --sensors 1 --sensor0-period-ratio 50 --readings danger after a Table 3 preset, i.e. one sensor that reports once at t=0. The source header calls it sound for a violation and only supporting evidence for a hold.

a timed hold in which the dangerous path was never taken: no rescue sent, or no reading read late. The binary prints a NOTE for it. All regime A cells are weak holds, and so is the B-safe cell; the holds of Table 3 rows 2, 3-6, 3-7 and 4 and the D-safe hold are not.
in cell names: FIRE = a violation exists (exit 101 without keep-going), HOLD = no violation in the explored state space.
in cell names: kg = --keep-going (explore everything, count the violations); p8, p16 = --parallel partitioned on 8 or 16 cores.
in cell names: the same arguments without keep-going; exit 101 with a printed witness timeline shows that the violation counted under keep-going is real.
a baseline-only cell run until the campaign deadline, to show that the baseline does not finish where the timed side does.
further event counters of the summary line: sensor checks that found a report, missions started, Acks handled before the ack timer, rescues sent, RescueReach handled before the rescue timer.

notes: Measured facts are taken from benchmarks/v9/results_v9.csv as it stood on 2026-10-11 11:09 (160 rows of this example, all finished, repetitions identical in complete, blocked and violating counts, timeline_impossible = 0 in every run) and from benchmarks/v8/results_v8.csv only for a side without a v9 row. Sides without a v9 result at that time: the baselines of the two Listing 6 random cells (rows 1 and 2), of the R=4 sensor cell and of the two ceilings, and the timed sides of the row 2 danger R=2 cell and of the R=6 edge rung.

Parameter columns: every value was resolved from the argument string with a transcription of the binary's parse_args and resolve (ratios times U, rounded) and agrees with every summary line of the example in results_v9.csv and results_v8.csv. A run that stops at a violation prints no summary line; the values of such cells rest on the same transcription, checked by one local run for the reduced model (S=1, P=100, C=1, Ds=4, Dr=6, OBST=1, timers separate). N (readings per sensor) is computed with the binary's formula, it is not printed.

Regimes: the letter fixes the network timing and the mission timers (L, U, sd, C, Ds, Dr, OBST); the sensor period P and the horizon R are given per cell. Rows 3-6 and 3-7 are on the safe side for R <= 3 and on the violating side at R = 4, hence two regime ids for one letter (I-safe / I-viol, J-safe / J-viol): the safe ones are bounded holds, not claims about the row. v8 used no regime letters for this example; A to K are new.
Table 3 has six presets, named 1, 2, 3-5, 3-6, 3-7 and 4 (there is no row 5, 6 or 7: 3-5, 3-6, 3-7 are row 3 with rescue deadline 5, 6 and 7). Row 3 at R=1 starts no mission and is not in the plan.

violation_counter is null: no summary counter equals the violating executions in every cell. dead and sensor_failures count events (missions, and sensor-check pairs), both are counted whatever --property asserts, and an execution is reported once even when both verdicts fail in it. Only for --property rescue at R=1 is dead the number of violating executions; those cells carry the extra field "violation_counter": "dead" (a per-cell hint, not part of FORMAT.md). It is equal on 10 of the 11 such sides measured in v9 (5 of them above zero). The exception is sensor-048-r1 (baseline of the row 4 danger cell, 8 worker threads, 1.15 billion explored): dead = 387,459,072 (also the v8 value, and equal to reached, as on every baseline side at R=1) against 387,459,038 failing-task lines, 34 fewer. That fits the merged output lines of a worker pool that build_v9_xlsx.py describes; the log is on the server and was not read. For that side dead is the exact count.

Complete executions include violating ones in this example. FORMAT.md and the comment at lines 1330 to 1332 of the source say that a violating execution is filed under blocked; the data say otherwise. The assertions are the Admin's last statements, after it has sent the Done messages, and under keep-going the search goes on past a failed assertion: an execution is complete exactly when every Done message is delivered (one in 4 with self timers, one in 16 with separate timers), whether or not an assertion failed in it. On all 37 finished keep-going sides of v9, complete = (checks_ok + sensor_failures) / (S x R) / 4 or 16. In the C-viol cell every mission is dead (missions = dead = 1,152 = violating executions) and 288 executions are complete: all of them violate. A local run of the one-sensor variant of that cell (not a campaign cell, binary of 30 September) gives the same complete and blocked counts with --property rescue (32 failing-task lines) and with --property sensor (none). So the violating executions are spread over the complete and the blocked columns, they can exceed the complete executions, and explored = complete + blocked still counts every execution once.

The baseline does not see the timing parameters: its complete, blocked and violating counts are identical across cells that differ only in U, L or a deadline (rows 1 and 2 with danger readings; the published P=6 cell and regimes B and C; the published R=3 sensor cell and regimes D and E). Only late_reports differs there, because that counter is computed from L.

kind: a cell is first-violation as soon as one of its sides runs without keep-going. That covers the five cells named 'exact: timed random-relevant kg vs baseline random', whose timed side is exhaustive (keep-going) and whose baseline side stops at its first violation; their two sides also differ in --readings, and the Readings column gives both values.

One-sided cells. (a) Two ceiling pairs: 'published timers, sensor property, S=2 R=5' and 'T3 row2 danger S=2 R=2' are each planned under two cell names, the timed run and, with '(baseline ceiling)' in the name, its baseline run with the same arguments; the two entries of a pair have the same regime, kind and parameters, so they can be shown as one row. The baseline of each is expected to run into the deadline. (b) Four exact pairs that are NOT the same instance run twice: row 4 R=1, row 2 R=2, rows 3-6 and 3-7 R=3. The timed cell runs random-relevant with keep-going on 8 cores, the baseline cell runs random without keep-going (1 core, or a 5-core pool for row 4); their Readings and kind differ on purpose so that they stay two rows. (c) The R=6 edge rung has a timed side only.

First-violation runs: the time to the first violation depends on the search order, which a random seed sets wherever the program calls nondet (random readings, the obstacle); Config::seed defaults to a fresh random number and the example has no --seed flag. The three timed repetitions of the row 1 Listing 6 cell took 194.3, 59.3, 133.0 s. Never compare the two sides on such a time.

The baseline row 4 random cell runs without keep-going under --parallel partitioned. There a worker that meets a violation stops alone, the others go on, and the failure is raised again after the pool has ended (traceforge/src/parallel_verify.rs: catch_unwind around each task, resume_unwind after the summary), so its wall time is not a time to the first violation, and its v9 row carries 155 failing-task lines although keep-going is off.

Ladders. Rounds R: published timers with the sensor property, R = 3, 4, 5, 6 on the timed side and R = 3, 4 plus the R=5 ceiling on the baseline; row 2 danger R = 1, 2. Readings per sensor N: the published model at N = 4, 5, 7 (P = 6, 5, 3), both sides finished. For the automatic ladder detection N is a size column marked moves_with_size (it follows R), and P is marked moves_with_size because lowering P is how N is raised. Not detected automatically: the timed exact rows (row 2: R = 1, 2; rows 3-6 and 3-7: R = 2, 3), because the Readings value of the two-sided cell names both sides; writing 'random-relevant' there would join them.
With safe readings (sensor-property cells) no mission starts: Ds, Dr, OBST and the timers mode are shown as the binary resolves them (default ratios times U) but have no effect.

sd = 0 in every cell, so the sd terms of the two laws are not exercised in v9. The grids that checked the laws (source header, 2026-09-16) used one sensor and predate the change that made every send lossy; v9 confirms the laws only at the cells of regimes B to K, with two sensors.

Deviations of the model from the paper that a citation should mention (source header): the first sensor check is at time C, not 0; the Rescue's message expiry is not modelled (it cannot bind in any Table 3 row); sensors send a bounded number of readings and never fail; at most two sensors; the drain rule; ties are explored in both orders.
